title: Supply chain hardening (npm hygiene + Claude Code hooks)
description: Harden the npm dependency surface and add the first Claude Code hooks for the harness. Motivated by the recent wave of npm supply-chain incidents (compromised maintainer accounts publishing malicious postinstall scripts, e.g. the s1ngularity / chalk-debug class of attacks). Adds three defensive layers: (1) `.npmrc` with `ignore-scripts=true`, `engine-strict=true`, and `minimum-release-age=7d` (npm 11.7+) — blocks the dominant attack vector and the recently-published-package window; (2) `npm audit` step in `init.sh` failing on moderate-or-higher, with the current 5 transitive CVEs resolved via `npm audit fix` and `overrides` where needed; (3) `.claude/settings.json` with hooks blocking out-of-band edits to `feature_list.json` and `package-lock.json`. Also pins Node/npm versions via `engines`, adds Dependabot config, documents the policy in `docs/conventions.md`, and updates `CHECKPOINTS.md`. Inserted at priority 0.5 — before `test-baseline` — so every subsequent feature inherits the hardening. RE-OPENED 2026-05-19 after the initial close: the Claude Code hooks shipped using a non-existent env var (`CLAUDE_TOOL_INPUT_FILE_PATH`) and therefore never blocked anything. The reviewer's verification was synthetic (set the variable manually and confirmed the bash branch executed) but not end-to-end (never confirmed that Claude Code actually populates that variable). The correct mechanism is stdin JSON parsed via `jq` against `.tool_input.file_path`. This re-open ships the corrected hook, adds a real end-to-end verification recipe to `reviewer.md`, and updates `leader.md` to reflect that status rotations in `feature_list.json` will go through `jq`-driven Bash from now on (the hook will block direct Edit|Write).
acceptance: `.npmrc` exists with `ignore-scripts=true`, `engine-strict=true`, `minimum-release-age=7d`, and a comment block documenting the rationale for each setting.
`package.json` has `engines: { node: ">=20", npm: ">=11.7" }` and an `overrides` block (if needed) closing the current moderate CVEs.

An allowlist mechanism exists for legitimate postinstall scripts (esbuild today). Approach is documented in `docs/conventions.md` — current preferred form: explicit `npm rebuild esbuild` step in `init.sh` after `npm ci --ignore-scripts`.

`init.sh` adds: (a) `npm --version >= 11.7` sanity check, (b) explicit `npm ci` with `ignore-scripts` honoured (relies on `.npmrc`), (c) `npm rebuild` for the allowlisted packages, (d) `npm audit --audit-level=moderate` step failing the build on findings.
`npm audit` returns 0 findings at moderate-or-higher after the feature lands (vulnerabilities resolved via patch-level upgrades and `overrides`, not by silencing).

`.claude/settings.json` exists with: `permissions.allow` for `npm *`, `npx *`, `./init.sh`, `jq *`, `git *`; `permissions.deny` for `Bash(rm -rf *)`; `PreToolUse` hooks blocking direct `Edit|Write` to `feature_list.json` and `package-lock.json` from any agent (these must change via the leader workflow / `npm install` respectively).
`.github/dependabot.yml` configured for `npm` ecosystem with weekly cadence and a grouping rule that bundles dev dependencies. Security updates open immediately regardless of cadence.

`docs/conventions.md` has a new section `Supply chain hygiene` codifying the policy (no manual `package-lock.json` edits, `ignore-scripts` default, audit threshold, allowlist procedure for postinstall, `minimum-release-age` rationale).
`docs/architecture.md` records the supply-chain decision under `Decisions to revisit` or a new dedicated section.

`CHECKPOINTS.md` adds a `Dependencies` block: (a) no new dependency without justification in the implementer's report, (b) `npm audit` step in `init.sh` is green, (c) any new postinstall script triggers an explicit allowlist update review.
`README.md` mentions the dependency policy briefly (one paragraph) and links to the conventions section.
`./init.sh` exits 0 after all of the above.

title: UI refresh and app-shell foundations
description: Port the UI work from the refactor-base branch into the post-harness main, adapting to MUI 6 / Vite 7 / Prettier / the new tests pipeline / no-socket.io / no-client-side-roomId. The refactor-base branch already contains an app-shell (Header + Drawer + Routes + Theme + UserContext + ToggleButton + custom icons + Error/WIP/NewGame/Play pages) but lives under the pre-harness monorepo layout and uses obsolete patterns (socket.io, ShortUniqueId for room ids). Scope: port the structural pieces, adopt them to current conventions, ship a custom dark-first theme (indigo + zinc + Inter), introduce react-router-dom v7 (new dep), extend UserContext to a discriminated union of guest/authenticated, retitle the product as 'Chess Room', and pay down the CustomDialog legacy debt (default export, missing Readonly<Props>). Page logic that depends on REST/STOMP stays stubbed with TODO(feature-N) markers per the existing pattern. Inserted at priority 3 so REST integrations (now 4-5) and live updates (now 6) land on the polished shell.
acceptance: react-router-dom v7 added as a dependency; npm audit clean at moderate+ after the install.
index.html: title 'Chess Room', favicon SVG (chess-room.svg or equivalent), meta description, theme-color, OG tags for previews.

Inter loaded via @fontsource/inter (subset latin); the loaded weights documented in the feature note.
main.tsx wraps the app in ThemeProvider (from @mui/material/styles, NOT @emotion/react) + CssBaseline + RouterProvider from react-router-dom.

title: STOMP subscription for real-time updates
description: Connect the STOMP client to the backend's broadcast topic for game state. After a move is submitted via REST, the server pushes the new state to all subscribers of /topic/games/{gameId}. The frontend subscribes and updates the local state accordingly. Depends on backend feature 6 (websocket-realtime) being shipped.
acceptance: STOMP client connects on Play page mount and disconnects on unmount.
